audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 fits 50.6% over 2587 games and a split chart: you own levels 2-5 on rotation strength, he owns 6 and his first lethality item, and the late game returns to you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven full-layer rows read 'Skill' while content win[] read Skill/Galio/Galio/Galio/Zed/Zed/Galio, and every why was the generic Galio template — including a level 6 row that claimed the map owed you taxes on the exact row Zed wins.
audit.why: The content layer matches packet.levelChart exactly. Zed's spikes are Death Mark at 6 (120s at rank 1) and his first lethality item; yours are the level 3 rotation and the two-item teamfight.
audit.corrected: Six sides moved onto the packet/content verdicts, ratings adjusted, all seven whys rewritten — one atomic group. win[] already holds the correct values.

audit.whatIsWrong: Slot confusion throughout the content layer: Living Shadow was called 'his shadow (E)' and 'his E-swap' when it is his W, and Razor Shuriken was called 'melee-range Q poke' when it reaches 900. Winds of War was credited with a knockup twice — Galio's Q is two windblasts converging into a tornado, and the knockup is Justice Punch.
audit.why: Zed kit: Q 900 projectile, W Living Shadow 650 dash on 20/19/18/17/16, E Shadow Slash 290 slow on 5/4.5/4/3.5/3, R Death Mark 625, untargetable, mark repeats damage after 3 seconds. Galio Q has only the projectile flag; E carries dash and the knockup.
audit.corrected: Every slot corrected, and the decisive timing stated: he is untargetable through the Death Mark dash, so the taunt is spent on his landing, not on the cast.

audit.why: The three numbers that matter are Death Mark 120s at rank 1, Living Shadow 20s at rank 1, and your own Shield of Durand at 18s — the taunt has to be available for the ult window or the window is free for him.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Check it before every step-up. - W Shield of Durand is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Zed Death Mark: 120s at rank 1 — he arrives untargetable, so save the taunt for the moment he lands, not the moment he presses it. - Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1. - Your W Shield of Durand is 18s: it has to cover the mark.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.
edits.after: Q from 825 at the contact and taunt only when the real Zed steps in — Shadow Slash is 290 range, so it has to touch you.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.

edits.before: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: He is untargetable through the dash — start the charge as he lands so the taunt catches the body, not the shadow.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.
edits.after: Q the shadow he swaps back to: the 20s Living Shadow only saves him once, and the tornado ticks on the ground he lands on.

edits.before: Zed whiffs Death Mark and the lane briefly belongs to you.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.
edits.after: Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1 — leaving without it means Zed takes the wave and you have no way back into the lane.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Zed wins by arriving untargetable with Death Mark, chunking you inside the 3-second mark, and never being where you swing.

edits.before: Carry through arrivals — Hero's Entrance turns every losing skirmish your team starts into a 5v4 with a knockup.
edits.after: Carry by arriving — Hero's Entrance lands with a knockup on the flank Zed picked, and the shield covers his burst.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared middle wave that keeps your R timer flexible — Galio waves are about being free to leave. Worst wave: a hard-shoved wave when your bot lane is fighting — the R you couldn't channel is the fight your team lost. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: a middle wave you can leave — Zed shoves with a 6s Razor Shuriken, so match him and keep the R timer free. Worst wave: a wave pushed past the river with Death Mark up, which is the exact picture he is waiting for. Crash timing: crash before you roam — the wave should be moving toward him whenever you are not in lane.

edits.before: Once you have your full combo, Zed's melee-range Q poke into shadow trades loses to your Winds of War knockup — he can't safely stack Q stacks on you without eating a stun.
edits.after: Once you have the full combo, Zed's shadow trades lose to Justice Punch — that is the knockup, not your Q, and he cannot step into Shadow Slash range without eating it.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is close to a coinflip since neither of you has a full combo, and Zed's early Q poke can chip you if you overextend for cs. From Level 3 you pull ahead in the trade — Winds of War punishes his shadow-swap approach with a knockup, and Shield of Durand blocks a big chunk of his burst, so he has to play passively and just farm.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is close to a coinflip since neither of you has a full combo, and his 900-range Razor Shuriken chips you if you overextend for cs. From Level 3 you pull ahead in the trade — Justice Punch punishes the shadow-swap approach with a knockup, and Shield of Durand blocks a big chunk of his burst, so he has to play passively and farm.

edits.before: You control Levels 4-5 through pure trade patterns: bait his E-swap in, knock him up, and follow with Justice Punch before he can reset the fight. That control evaporates the second he hits Level 6 — Zed's ultimate lets him swap onto you from a shadow and burst you down in under two seconds, so treat Levels 6-7 as a landmine and play with vision and spacing rather than trading freely.
edits.after: You control Levels 4-5 through pure trade patterns: bait the Living Shadow swap in, knock him up with Justice Punch, and taunt before he can reset the fight. That control evaporates the second he hits Level 6 — Death Mark brings him in untargetable and repeats his damage after 3 seconds, so treat Levels 6-7 as a landmine and play with vision and spacing rather than trading freely.

notes: The content layer had Zed's slots wrong in three places — Living Shadow described as 'his shadow (E)' and 'his E-swap' when it is his W, and Razor Shuriken called 'melee-range Q poke' when it reaches 900 — plus two claims that Winds of War knocks him up, when Galio's knockup is Justice Punch. All corrected.
